content: Hi ! This is my first contribution (puzzle) so if there's any problem then... leave a comment ! (And I think it's a little bit "Easy", if yes then I will retry another 😊).

The puzzle is too easy and there are already a number of clashes on the same theme of Collatz conjecture.

Please use another idea for your contribution. Thanks.
Ok, so I finished, if there's other problems then leave a comment.

Goal
* Please move the last sentence to the beginning.

* Please change all {{constant}} format to <<bold>>.

* Please format 0, 1, 8 and 9 as {{constants}}.

* Please remove the quotation marks in 'A “signal”'.

* Please change "When" to "Every time".

* Please change "      °" to "　°" (a full-width space), as leading ordinary spaces are ignored and cannot be used for indentation.

* Please add "." after "resets to 0".

* Please add "except previously overloaded cells" after "(including diagonals)".

* Please change "diagonals" to "horizontal, vertical and diagonal". (Remember to remove "s" from "diagonals".)

* Please insert the following paragraph immediately before "Your task":

If several cells overload simultaneously, they may be processed in any order and should give the same result.

Input
* Line 1: Please add "space-separated" after "Two".

* Next H lines: Please add "representing one row of the grid" at the end.

* Next line: Please add "space-separated" after "Two".

* Next line: Please add "the row and column indexes (0-based) of" before "the starting cell".

Constraints
* Please change 50 to 10.

* Please remove "0 ≤ grid values ≤ 9".

Stub generator
* Please change 50 to W.

Tags
* Please remove "Chain Reaction", "Logic" and "Propagation".

Cases
* After updating the stub generator, please click "TEST IN IDE". You'll be notified that, in the "No Overload" test, each grid row contains more than W characters. Please change W to 3.

* Each test and its validator should cover the *same scenario* with slightly different inputs and outputs. So, please convert each test into a pair of cases as described below.

* Test 1: Revise the input to demonstrate more clearly the effect of an overload on both neighbouring and non-neighbouring cells:

5 5
00000
08120
07930
06540
00000
2 2

* Validator 1: Use the same input as above, except that the ring of digits surrounding the centre increases counter-clockwise.

* Use the existing cases (excluding Wave Expansion and Complex Cascade) as follows:

  • Test 2: Full Overload

  • Test 3: Chain Reaction, modified so that R > C

  • Test 4: Diagonal Chain, modify the grid so that W < H, make R < C (e.g. 0 2), and replace all 8s with 9s

  • Test 5: No Overload, replace both 1s with 9s, and keep W > H and the starting cell at (0, 0)

  • Test 6: Large Calm Zone, keep the starting cell at bottom-right corner

* Create new Validators 2 to 6, each matching its respective test with slight variations.

* Please use the code here ( https://pastebin.com/2Dc75k0J ) to generate two new pairs of cases:

  • Test/Validator 7: H = W = 8

  • Test/Validator 8: H = W = 10

Thanks.
Ok finished (except first of the generator of stub because it will make an error and the Test cases because I don't want to modifide them).

Which is why I included this point:

The case is wrong. Updating the stub generator helps you catch such errors.
I can't because if it's 3 then there will be 5 errors: Chain Reaction, Diagonal Chain, Large Calm Zone, Wave Expantion and Complex Cascade 😢.

I'm not sure what you did 😅 But I just updated both the stub generator and the case, and everything went through without any errors.

Could you please follow up the remaining outstanding points?
